newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares fall as foreign buying eases.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares fall as foreign buying eases.

text.p: Jordan's official stock market index fell for a fourth day running on Wednesday in quiet trade after foreign demand for shares eased, brokers said.
The official Amman market's 60-share index fell 0.13 percent to 165.73 points after the lowest turnover for over a month worth just 580,000 dinars ($820,000).
The index was pushed to three-year highs on Saturday on the back of high demand for the market-moving shares of Arab Bank, which themselves hit a five-year peak.
But the shares have fallen since then as an anticipated cabinet approval of a law scrapping foreign ownership ceilings in Jordanian stock failed to materialise.
The bank's foreign ownership stake is already over the existing 50 percent maximum and a lifting of the ceiling is expected to unleash further international buying.
On Wednesday the stock fell 0.50 dinars to 289.50 dinars in trade worth 132,000 dinars.
Broker Ibrahim Odeh said Arab Bank's fall and local investors' caution ahead of expected half-year results had left the market in the doldrums.
Falling shares outnumbered gainers on Wednesday by 16 to nine, with another 23 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fell 0.19 percent to 80.80 points. It is 3.11 percent down from the start of the year.
